No, the bank cannot execute on the whole property. Under the majority lien-theory rule, the mortgage is only a lien on the borrower's joint-tenancy interest and does not sever the tenancy, so his death extinguishes the lien and the survivor takes the house free of it. The team note is wrong: the rule that a mortgage transfers title and severs the joint tenancy is the minority title-theory view, not the majority view.

CONFIDENCE: 70
